fe  5.  CITY COUNCILISTAFF COMMENTS
_  Councilmember Devine attended several events these past two weeks. She
  congratulated the Montrose Verdugo Craft Beer Fest 2023 for a well-attended event.
  Devine and Mayor Brotman attended the Home Again LA fundraiser. The organization
  helps victims of domestic violence who are on the verge of homelessness. She
  congratulated CEO Albert Hernandez for a very successful event.

  Councilmember Kassakhian visited the Verdugo Hills Boys Scout Rocket Academy
  Camp. He also attended the Filipino American Friendship Monument’s 1° Year
  Anniversary event together with the Philippine Consul General. He congratulated
  everyone involved in organizing the event. Kassakhian congratulated city staff for
  organizing all the events leading up to the commemoration of the Armenian Genocide. It
  was also the one-year anniversary of the Armenian film. The Genocide commemoration
  event at the Alex Theatre included the showing of clips from films that addressed the
  topics of the Armenian Genocide, Armenian survival, and the ongoing attempt at
  genocide in the region of Artsakh. Councilmember Kassakhian mentioned one of the film
  being Aurora’s Sunrise

  Councilmember Asatryan attended the Earth Day Event at Pacific Park. She
  recommended having the event in the future at a location that has more foot traffic,
  specifically the Americana at Brand, to attract more attendees. She gave kudos to the
  Adams Hill Association for hosting an Earth Day event in their neighborhood. Asatryan
ie.
  announced the month of May is “Mental Health Awareness” Month. For mental health
  support, the public can call #988. She announced that the city’s 1° Annual Small
 ——e
|
 A
  Business Summit is coming up on May 16-18 and invited the public to go to
  www.chooseglendale.com for more information. The highlight of the event was an
  interview with Joe Manganiello who spoke about his Armenian heritage.

  Mayor Brotman attended the Montrose Wine Walk where customers sample wines from
  various pour stations hosted by Montrose merchants and businesses. He thanked
  Elizabeth Harris from the Sustainability Division for holding a discussion at the Glendale
  Centrai Library called “Carbon Conversations.” Brotman stated that Ted Flanigan, a
  previous GWP  Commissioner, also spoke at the Glendale Central Library on clean
  energy resources. Mayor Brotman also attended the Kiwanis Duck Splash at the
  Verdugo Park and the Solar Fair presented by the Sustainability Division and GWP held
  at Roosevelt Middle School. Brotman spoke about participating in a program with
  GUSD called “Principal for a Day” at the Verdugo Woodiands Elementary School.
  Brotman announced that he is the city representative for the newly formed agency
  called the Burbank Glendaie Pasadena Regional Housing Trust. The state has
  allocated $23M to the trust to help finance affordable housing projects in the three cities
  through the Joint Powers Authority outlined by Senator Portantino’s $B177.

  Director of Community Development Bradley Calvert introduced the new Building
  Official, Ara Sargsyan and thanked Miroslav Lhotsky for stepping in as interim Building
  Official prior to Sargsyan’s appointment. Calvert provided a brief presentation on the
  Land Management System program. Assistant Chief Information Officer Hagop
i  Hovsepian provided a brief presentation on the new Glendale Permits program.
